title: A Banana Is a Berry. A Strawberry Is Not.
hook: A banana is a berry, and a strawberry is not.
script: A banana is a berry, and a strawberry is not. That is not a joke, it is how botany sorts fruit. A berry grows from one flower, has soft flesh, and keeps its seeds inside. So why does a strawberry fail the test? Its seeds sit on the outside, stuck to the skin. The red flesh grows from the base of the flower, not from the part that holds the seeds. So what else counts as a berry? Grapes, tomatoes and avocados. Raspberries and blackberries fail too, because each one is a cluster of tiny fruits. In the supermarket, the name on the label and the botany rarely agree.
